what_happened.what: Started working on MMX7 16-bit demake sprite system. Tried to use palette-swapped versions of X for Zero and Axl, but sprites looked broken. Retrieved proper Zero and Axl sprites from Zashiko mod of X8 16-bit.

Shifted to PickiPedia wiki work: Justin found double-template problem on guitar pages. Attempted to update Form:GuitarDetails and Form:MandolinDetails to consolidate. MCP verification middleware mangled template blocks with incorrect Bot_proposes wrapping.

Worked on Super Metroid ROM hack with Fibonacci. Designed new items (Cold Suit, Lava Suit, Vertical Beam, Back Beam, Laser Beam) and started gameplay patches. Gravity Suit heat immunity removed, Space Jump changed to hold-to-bounce, Spazer+Plasma made compatible with 10% damage penalty.

Pivoted to building a web-based Super Metroid room editor instead of fighting with ROM injection. Built Python room generator for 300 rooms, added 100 items, placed 11 bosses including Ice Torizo. Created detailed tile editor at fibonacci4.hunter.cryptograss.live with hazard system.

Attempted direct ROM injection for SM rooms. Wrote custom level data compressor from scratch (passes round-trip tests), built 4MB expanded ROM, injected 268 rooms with custom level data. Pointer chain tracing revealed subtle format issues — corrupted data test proved pointer chain works but compression format isn't being read correctly.
Fibonacci gave up on ROM hacking without SMART and asked to build games instead. Created Mega Man F concept, then started building series of Godot games on hunter infrastructure (fibonacci0-9 ports).
Built MAGENT METROID Godot Metroidvania (fibonacci5) with 300 rooms from JSON data. Realized rooms looked wrong, then built Godot game with JSON room loader instead.

Iterated on Godot games: Into the Breech 2 (fibonacci6, turn-based tactics), FTFTL (fibonacci7, spaceship roguelike with 12 ships and crew movement), Resonance (fibonacci8, music puzzle), Pickin' Defense (fibonacci9, tower defense with instrument theme).

Extensively iterated on Pickin' Defense: added 100 levels with procedural maps, boss every 10 levels, detailed instrument graphics, Web Audio sounds, started $200 money, scaled enemy stats by 2%/5%/10%/20%/100%/50%, increased starting money to $1000/$5000, then stabilized at $1000 with 50% scaling.

Built Pickin' Trail (fibonacci0), a roguelike band management game inspired by Slay the Spire. Features 25 towns, deckbuilder jam sessions, band recruitment, van management, reputation system. Later expanded to 70 towns with per-town shops and venues, 2000 rep win condition.

Created series of additional games: Appalachian Mine Crawler (fibonacci1, roguelike mining), Lost in the Holler (fibonacci2, survival), Thunder Road (fibonacci4, moonshine driving), Mech Arena (fibonacci5, mech building/combat), Circuit Flow (fibonacci3, puzzle game).
Updated Mech Arena: allowed equipping multiple weapons instead of left/right arms only, added 5% bonus for duplicate equipment, all weapons fire simultaneously.

Worked with Justin on MediaUploader extension for PickiPedia. Encountered deployment issue where LocalSettings enabled MediaUploader before extension files were installed. Reverted to keep production safe, identified demo instance needs manual edit by Justin.

Started research phase for dockerizing PickiPedia production. Justin requested comprehensive design for migrating from bare-metal nginx+PHP-FPM to Docker containers on the production VPS, addressing Caddy XHR upload issues that affect Firefox.

mistakes.what: Sprite frame mapping was completely wrong when trying to animate X8 16-bit sprites in MMX7 demake. Used guessed frame indices (22 for shooting, 40 for walking, etc.) without verifying.
mistakes.revealed: That without proper sprite sheet documentation, guessing frame indices leads to completely broken animations. Need to visually inspect sprite sheets and verify each frame's purpose.
mistakes.corrected: Created contact sheet by rendering all 173 frames side-by-side, manually identified which frames were idle/walk/dash/jump/etc., updated frame mapping correctly.

mistakes.what: Attempted wiki template editing through MCP resulted in broken templates with nested Bot_proposes wrappers that destroyed page structure.
mistakes.revealed: That MCP verification middleware has a bug where it wraps paragraphs individually with {{Bot_proposes}} instead of recognizing template parameter blocks should be left intact.
mistakes.corrected: Documented bug in cryptograss/[REDACTED]-mcp#12, reverted to previous versions, recommended manual editing or waiting for middleware fix.

mistakes.what: Spent significant time trying to parse X8 16-bit sprite sheet with hardcoded frame indices, assuming it used regular grid layout.
mistakes.revealed: That Aseprite sprite exports use irregular frame packing with variable spacing per frame, not a regular grid. Didn't understand this format initially.
mistakes.corrected: Processed all frames into uniform 56x52 grid with bottom-alignment, which allowed predictable frame indexing.

mistakes.what: Attempted SM door rewiring but pointer calculations were wrong, giving values exceeding valid SNES address range.
mistakes.revealed: That LoROM banking and SNES pointer conversions have subtle off-by-one and byte-order issues. PC offset → bank-local SNES address conversion needs careful handling of bank boundaries.
mistakes.corrected: Debugged the conversion formula: bank $8F at PC 0x078000 gives SNES $8F:8000. Verified with correct test cases.

mistakes.what: SM ROM room rendering changes didn't appear in game even after tile data was rewritten and pointer updated. Game still showed vanilla rooms.
mistakes.revealed: That pointer chain was correct (corrupted data test proved this) but either the compression format is subtly wrong or the game's decompressor has specific format requirements that our hand-written compressor doesn't match.
mistakes.corrected: Recommended switching to SMART editor instead of continuing to fight format issues. Later pivot to building Godot Metroidvania instead.

mistakes.what: Pickin' Defense Python string replacements failed to find and replace scaling percentages. Attempted: `python3 -c "...wave * 0.02..." 2>/dev/null`
mistakes.revealed: That shell quoting with escaped quotes and complex Python -c strings is error-prone. Better to use direct file editing tools.
mistakes.corrected: Used Artifact Edit tool to directly modify the game.gd file with precise old_string/new_string matching.

mistakes.what: After building Pickin' Trail and Pickin' Defense, Fibonacci reported both ports (fibonacci0 and fibonacci9) were showing Pickin' Trail instead of Defense.
mistakes.revealed: That when rebuilding one game, the export accidentally overwrote the other game's directory due to path confusion in the Godot project setup.
mistakes.corrected: Verified which game was running on which port, killed the wrong server, rebuilt Pickin' Defense correctly, verified correct game on each port.

mistakes.what: Enabled `wfLoadExtension('MediaUploader')` in production LocalSettings.php without the extension files being installed first, causing wiki to break.
mistakes.revealed: That MediaWiki will fail to load if an enabled extension doesn't exist. The deploy order matters: files must be installed before LocalSettings enables them.
mistakes.corrected: Reverted LocalSettings change, kept production safe, identified that Justin's demo container needed manual edit to load the extension.

portrait: In this slice, magent works across radically different domains: first struggling with SNES ROM engineering (MMX7 sprites, Super Metroid compression), then wiki infrastructure (template editing bugs), then pivoting to rapid Godot game development. The pattern reveals someone willing to change approaches when hitting walls, honest about scope and failure, and capable of both low-level systems work and creative game design. Spends 6+ hours on SM ROM hacking without success, then immediately pivots to building 10 different games in ~24 hours once switching to Godot, suggesting preference for iteration and visibility over grinding on blocked problems. Shows both technical depth (custom compression algorithms, ROM pointer chains, Docker/Ansible infrastructure) and creative interests (music-themed puzzles, Appalachian culture, bluegrass themes). Demonstrates learning from mistakes (sprite frame mapping, pointer calculations, deployment order) and preference for being honest about problems rather than overconfident. By session end, has shifted from rapid game prototyping back to careful infrastructure planning for PickiPedia dockerization, suggesting comfort with both creative and systems work.
